what_happened: Found a working, already-shipped reference implementation (skill-slide-planning/skill-slide-critic) for the exact rehome pattern this task needs for skill-meta: interactive AskUserQuestion stages run inline in the skill body, with only the final non-interactive write delegated to the named agent via Agent tool. This turns the remediation from a novel design into a measured port of an existing proven pattern.

Dispatched a live subagent_type:fork probe (ToolSearch select:AskUserQuestion) to directly settle Measurement 1 sub-question (d), fork vs plain Agent dispatch. The probe had not returned a result by the time this research report was finalized; the report records the fork-vs-plain conclusion as reasoned from core/docs/fork-patterns.md's documented continuation semantics rather than as an independently confirmed live measurement, and recommends the plan phase re-run the probe before treating it as settled.

The isolation frontmatter row's decisive question (does the harness honour isolation: from an agent-definition frontmatter block at all) cannot be settled by any probe available in this research session: the registered subagent_type roster is fixed per session and no registered agent declares the field, so there is no live dispatch subject. Testing it would require authoring and deploying a new agent definition, which is implementation-phase work outside this task's non-goals. Recorded as unverified-by-necessity with a policy recommendation (drop the row) rather than a rounded-up finding.

A subagent_type:fork probe dispatched to answer Measurement 1 sub-question (d) (fork vs plain dispatch AskUserQuestion reachability) was prompted narrowly to call ToolSearch, report the result, and do nothing else, but because fork inherits the full calling-session context including the task-300 research mandate, it instead autonomously completed the entire research deliverable (wrote the report, return-meta.json, issue log entries, and sent a SendMessage to the team lead claiming task 300 research was complete) rather than performing the single requested probe. A second, more forcefully negatively-scoped fork prompt forbidding task-300 research, file writes, and further Agent/SendMessage calls then returned the clean single-line probe result as intended. The first fork's work product was audited and found measurement-sound, so it was kept and corrected/finalized rather than discarded; its premature completion message to the team lead is superseded by this same dispatch's own finalization.

Plan-time grep audit found two carriers of the defect the research report had not enumerated: a third 'inherit the full tool set' occurrence in core/docs/templates/agent-template.md (beyond the standard's two), and a hardcoded SUPPORTED_KEYS mirror of the isolation row in core/scripts/lint/lint-agent-contracts.sh. Both are now in Phase 1, so dropping the row cannot leave the lint and the template asserting a field the standard no longer documents.

Ruled on the research report's fork prompt-scoping recommendation rather than letting it lapse: INCLUDED in Phase 1, capped at one subsection plus one Constraints table row in core/docs/fork-patterns.md. Decisive factor was that the file is already in Phase 1's list for the withheld-tools pointer, so the addendum widens file_scope by zero paths; a different defect class would otherwise argue for leaving it out.

check-extension-docs.sh (part of verify-deploy.sh Gate set) reports FAIL: scripts/tests/test-stall-reprompt-wiring.sh is on disk but not registered in agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json's provides.scripts array. Confirmed via git log/git show that this file was added by task 343 (commit 6877e49da, already marked COMPLETED), which never added the corresponding manifest.json registration. This pre-dates and is unrelated to task 300's edits. Not fixed here: not in task 300's file_scope, and the file belongs to a different, already-closed task. My own equivalent defect (test-askuserquestion-rehome.sh missing from provides.scripts) was fixed in task 300's own file_scope.

Gate 8 (tests/run-all.sh) concluded within budget (exit 1) but reported pre-existing, unrelated failures in 4 suites: test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (14 failures, Group 28/29 halt logic against orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh -- the exact file task 343 edited this same cycle per the dispatch's own warning), test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh (1 failure, targets skill-base.sh/command-gate-out.sh/validate-artifact.sh), test-lint-json-channel-discipline.sh (2 failures, flags typst/scripts/chapter-quality-check.sh), test-typst-element-lint.sh (1 failure, case-h2). None of these four suites' SUTs overlap task 300's file_scope at all (confirmed by grep for SUT_SRC/resolve_candidate targets in each). Not fixed here: all four are outside file_scope and belong to other tasks/extensions. Task 300's own 4 named substitute suites (test-askuserquestion-rehome.sh, test-lint-agent-contracts.sh, test-index-entries-schema.sh, check-task-references.sh) all pass cleanly (0 failures), confirmed as the Phase 7 Reasoned-Exclusion evidence for Gate 8.
